# Bootstrapping experiments {#sec-bootstrapping}

::: {.callout-note}
## Draft — results being finalized
The ladder below is current as of the latest runs (all-data, Gemini gold, Konkle test-60,
3 seeds). The **frame-MIL** rung and the full error-barred waterfalls are still being computed;
numbers and figures will be locked when those land.
:::

The question of this book is whether word–object mapping can be **bootstrapped** from naturalistic
data — whether a learner can climb from naive contrastive training toward the ceiling using only
signal it could plausibly have. This chapter maps that climb with a single, systematic design:
train on **all** of BabyView, evaluate on the out-of-sample **Konkle** benchmark (@sec-pipeline),
and measure what each mechanism contributes against oracle toplines.

## Three bootstraps

Every mechanism here is a form of *self-supervised selection* — deciding what to attend to
without being told the answer — at a different grain:

- **Region** (MIL max over frame cells): *where* in the frame is the referent.
- **Frame** (MIL max over a ±2 s window): *which moment* shows it best.
- **Utterance** (EM reweighting of pairs by self-estimated alignment): *which pairs* are aligned.

The oracles that bound them are **alignment** (which pairs are truly referential) and the
**referent label** (which word names the object) — both from the Gemini annotation of @sec-data.

## The ladder

Region-MIL learner, Konkle test-60, mean ± sd over 3 seeds:

| Rung | Konkle | Δ | kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| chance | 25 | — | — |
| pure learning (whole-frame, noisy data) | 52.1 ± 1.9 | +27 | free |
| **+ region MIL** | 62.6 ± 1.7 | **+10.5** | free (architecture) |
| + alignment filter | 68.5 ± 1.3 | +5.9 | oracle |
| + word selection | 73.2 ± 1.2 | +4.7 | oracle |
| + vision-binding | 81.3 ± 2.6 | +8.1 | oracle |
| ceiling | ~81 | — | +18.7 unlearnable from these features |

Two facts frame everything that follows. **Region MIL is free and large (+10.5):** picking the
best-matching cell of a frame, with no labels, does implicit referent localization and lands the
unaided learner at **62.6**. Above that, every rung is currently an **oracle** — it requires
information (which pairs are aligned; which word is the referent) we do not have at training time.
The bootstrapping problem is precisely whether accessible signal can climb those rungs.

## What the bootstraps buy

**Utterance (EM).** The self-supervised EM loop — reweighting pairs by the model's own
max-region alignment — is the direct attempt to climb the *filter* rung without the oracle. It
does almost nothing: **+1.8** without MIL, **+0.9** with it (seed 0; error bars pending). It does
not ignite, and MIL has already absorbed most of what it targets.

**Region.** Not really a bootstrap so much as the architecture, but it is the single biggest free
gain (+10.5), and it is why the filter oracle is worth only ~+6 on top: much of "which pairs are
aligned" is recovered by "which cell matches."

**Frame.** *(In progress.)* Does selecting the best frame in a ±2 s window add anything beyond
region selection? Measured as a region × frame 2×2 on matched data.

## The label decomposition

The largest oracle gap is the referent *label* (+18.7 to Topline-2). Holding the pair set fixed,
it splits cleanly into three comparable pieces (region-MIL, 3 seeds):

| step | Konkle | Δ | isolates |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 62.6 | — | — |
| filtered-natural | 68.5 | +5.9 | which pairs |
| referent word *where spoken* | 73.2 | +4.7 | which word |
| referent word *always* | 81.3 | +8.1 | referent when unspoken (vision) |

The referent is actually spoken in only ~63% of aligned pairs; supplying it for the **unspoken**
37% is the single largest lever (+8.1), because those pairs otherwise carry no referential signal
at all. This is why @sec-cues aims cues at *identifying the referent* — including visually, when
it isn't said — rather than merely filtering frames.
